vocabulary.meaning: a person who rides a bicycle
examples: Cyclists need safe space on busy roads.
The driver waited until it was safe to pass the cyclist.

vocabulary.meaning: protective equipment worn on the head
examples: A helmet can reduce the risk of serious head injury.
The child always wears a helmet when cycling.

vocabulary.meaning: a part of the road or path intended for bicycles
examples: Protected cycle lanes can improve safety.
Cars should not park in the cycle lane.

vocabulary.meaning: how easily someone or something can be seen
examples: Bright clothing improves cyclist visibility at night.
Poor weather can reduce visibility.
Many cycling collisions happen at junctions.
Drivers should check carefully for cyclists at a junction.

vocabulary.meaning: the legal right to go first in a traffic situation
examples: Learn who has right of way at crossings and junctions.
Confusion about right of way can cause accidents.

vocabulary.meaning: able to send light back and therefore be easier to see
examples: Reflective clothing is useful after dark.
The bicycle has reflective strips on the wheels.

vocabulary.meaning: to pass a slower vehicle or cyclist travelling in the same direction
examples: Drivers should leave enough space when overtaking cyclists.
Do not overtake near a blind corner.

vocabulary.meaning: an accident in which vehicles, cyclists, or objects hit each other
examples: Safe road design can reduce collisions.
The cyclist avoided a collision by braking quickly.

vocabulary.meaning: any person who uses a road, including drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians
examples: All road users have responsibilities.
Road design should protect vulnerable road users.
